scope: Three bounded temporal-repair attempts on the geometry-approved frames 182-270 window
summary: Temporal repair raised the proxy above 0.75, but independent post-repair SAM2 tracking exposed contact and geometry regressions in the first three variants. None was promoted, and thresholds were not lowered.
evidence: strict-object-gate-v3 rejects the strong encoded variant at 36/39 for lower-hand centroid step, lime adjacent-area ratio, and lower-hand-to-lime p90 contact distance.
strict-object-gate-v4 rejects the balanced encoded variant at 36/39 for lime adjacent-area ratio and lower-hand-to-lime maximum and p90 contact distances.

Remote lossless regeneration in strict-object-gate-v5 reaches 38/39 with motion 0.841135, identity 0.979982, and temporal consistency 0.781989, but lower-hand-to-lime p90 distance is 9.510 pixels against the unchanged 8-pixel gate.
The trained FlowerRepairPolicy ranks local EPL crossfade/flow repairs over global smoothing, but final promotion is controlled by re-tracked object/contact gates rather than the proxy ranking.
lessons: Passing an aggregate temporal metric is insufficient: even source-local pixel repair can move a thin stem/contact boundary enough to violate strict interaction geometry.
Post-repair flower and hand tracks must be recomputed; carrying forward pre-repair masks would hide the regression.
limitations: These three variants are rejected and must not be used in the full film.
The repair remains an image-space temporal correction, not a learned 3-D dynamics model.
next_actions: Increase the exact contact-protection band and rerun the least destructive policy rounds, then independently re-track and re-evaluate all gates.
